instruction.text: Decide whether the present, past or future perfect tense fits best in the sentence.

atoms.b: The criminal ((has_vanished ++had_vanished will_have_vanished)) before we could call the police.
I ((have_learnt ++had_learnt will_have_learnt)) to write my name by the time I was three.
Lucy ((++has_come had_come will_have_come)) round to my house every day this week so far.
Martin ((has_worked had_worked ++will_have_worked)) for three companies by next month.

instruction.text: Fill in the gaps with the present perfect form of the verbs.

atoms.b: I ((have_danced)) at my dance school for ten years.
Ethan ((has_sung)) at five school concerts now.

feedback.wrong: The verb 'to sing' is irregular. For the present perfect tense, you need the past participle form of 'to sing'.

instruction.text: Fill in the gaps with the past perfect form of the verbs.

atoms.b: Tyler ((had_lied)) to his mum about his test result.
We ((had_brought)) food to share at the party.

feedback.wrong: The verb 'to bring' is irregular. For the past perfect tense, you need the past participle form of 'to bring'.

instruction.text: Fill in the gaps with the future perfect form of the verbs.

atoms.b: Daisy ((will_have_climbed)) Snowdon before she climbs Ben Nevis.
Josie ((will_have_met)) my family a few times by next week.

feedback.wrong: The verb 'to meet' is irregular. For the future perfect tense, you need the past participle form of 'to meet'.
